svg.title: DN 22 Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta — The Greater Discourse on the Establishments of Mindfulness
svg.desc: A memory map of DN 22: the four establishments of mindfulness, six body contemplations, felt experience, sixteen mind-states, hindrances, aggregates, sense bases, awakening factors, and the expanded Four Noble Truths with the Eightfold Path and four jhānas.

g.text: The Greater Discourse on the Establishments of Mindfulness
“This is the direct way, bhikkhus, for the purification of beings, for the overcoming of sorrow and lamentation,
for the subsiding of discomfort and distress, for the attainment of the right path, for the realization of Nibbāna”
ekāyano ayaṁ, bhikkhave, maggo sattānaṁ visuddhiyā · nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya
FOUR ESTABLISHMENTS OF MINDFULNESS · cattāro satipaṭṭhānā
With continuous effort, clearly aware and with excellent recollection, having removed craving and distress with regard to the world
ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ
Dwells observing the body in and of itself
Breathes mindfully; discerns long and short breaths;
trains to experience the whole body
When walking, standing, sitting, or lying down,
he discerns it accordingly. In whatever way the
body is oriented, he discerns it.
Acts with clear awareness going forward and
returning, looking, bending, wearing robes, eating,
Reviews the body from the soles upwards and hair
downwards as full of various impurities: skin, flesh, sinews,
bones, organs, stomach contents, fat, grease, and fluids.
Simile: bag with two openings full of many sorts of grains
in terms of the four elements:
like a butcher dividing a cow at a crossroads.
‘This body too is of the same nature;’
Dwells observing the felt experience in and of itself
Dwells observing the mind in and of itself
Discerns as it actually is — yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti

text.tspan: · yathā ca anuppannānaṁ nīvaraṇānaṁ uppādo hoti
④ how arisen hindrance is abandoned
· yathā ca uppannānaṁ nīvaraṇānaṁ pahānaṁ hoti
⑤ how abandoned hindrance does not arise again
· yathā ca pahīnassa nīvaraṇassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti

g.text: 4b. FIVE AGGREGATES SUBJECT TO CLINGING · pañcupādānakkhandhā
Discerns with regard to the aggregate:
4c. SIX INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL SENSE BASES · saḷāyatana
Dwells discerning the internal and external sense base and:

text.tspan: ① the fetter that arises dependent on both
③ how arisen fetter is abandoned
④ how it does not arise again

g.text: 4d. SEVEN FACTORS OF AWAKENING · satta bojjhaṅgā

text.tspan: Discerns when a factor of awakening is:
· yathā ca anuppannassa bojjhaṅgassa uppādo hoti
④ how arisen factor reaches fulfillment through cultivation
· yathā ca uppannassa bojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūrī hoti

g.text: Dwells observing the mental qualities in and of themselves with regard to the Four Noble Truths
Discerns as it actually is — yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti
This is the arising of suffering
This is the end of suffering
This is the way of practice
leading to the end of suffering
The first recitation section is completed · paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito
4.5.1 EXPOSITION OF THE TRUTH OF SUFFERING · dukkhasaccaniddesa
And what, bhikkhus, is the noble truth of suffering?
Not getting what one wants · yampicchaṁ na labhati
“Oh, may we not be subject to birth, aging, illness, death, and sorrow” — this cannot be attained by wishing
In brief, the five aggregates subject to clinging are suffering
saṅkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā dukkhā · rūpa · vedanā · saññā · saṅkhārā · viññāṇa
4.5.2–3 ARISING AND ENDING OF SUFFERING · samudaya · nirodha
Craving which leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and passion, seeking delight here and there
Whatever in the world appears dear and agreeable — here this craving arises and settles; here it is abandoned and ceases
When arising, arises; when become established, it is established
When being abandoned, is abandoned; when ceasing, it ceases
* craving can arise and settle for craving itself (in another being)
The remainderless fading away and ending of that very craving — giving up, relinquishing, release, non-attachment
4.5.4 THE WAY OF PRACTICE · dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā
It is just this Noble Eightfold Path · ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo
taking what is not given, sexual misconduct
earns a living by right livelihood
joy and pleasure born of seclusion
purity of mindfulness due to equanimity
without clinging to anything in the world · na ca kiñci loke upādiyati
Observing the arising nature, vanishing nature, or both
With mindfulness established, dwells independent, and without clinging
sati paccupaṭṭhitā · anissito ca viharati · na ca kiñci loke upādiyati
Whoever develops these four establishments of mindfulness,
one of two fruits may be expected, in as little as seven days, months, and years:
“This is the direct way, bhikkhus, for…”
